strengths_deep_dive: Intercultural Networks, Inc. demonstrates resilience through its <cite id="1">5.2 months of working capital</cite>, which is a healthy reserve for an organization of its size. This financial stability is supported by a <cite id="2">3-year revenue CAGR of 10.7%</cite>, showing consistent growth in donor support. Furthermore, the organization has achieved a <cite id="1">score of 100 in the Culture & Community beacon</cite> from Charity Navigator, suggesting strong internal alignment and leadership engagement. Its <cite id="1">Leadership score of 94.53</cite> also points to a well-structured executive vision, even as the financial execution remains a point of concern.
rich_narrative.summary: Intercultural Networks, Inc. (ING) operates as a religious and cultural organization focused on <cite id="1">promoting understanding and countering bigotry</cite> through educational seminars and panels. While the organization has a long operational history, its financial profile presents significant concerns for donors prioritizing direct service delivery. In 2023, the organization reported <cite id="2">total revenue of $622,869</cite>, yet it allocated a remarkably low portion of its budget to its core mission. Specifically, the <cite id="1">program expense ratio is 39.5%</cite>, meaning less than forty cents of every dollar spent actually reaches its educational programs. This figure is significantly below the standard benchmark for efficient non-profits. Despite these spending inefficiencies, the organization maintains a <cite id="1">Charity Navigator score of 86.0/100</cite>, bolstered by high marks in leadership and culture. However, the <cite id="1">accountability and finance beacon score of 86.77</cite> reflects the underlying fiscal challenges. ING does demonstrate some administrative strengths, such as <cite id="1">high fundraising efficiency</cite>, spending $0.00 to raise every $1. The organization also maintains <cite id="2">$271,576 in total assets</cite>, providing a modest financial cushion. For donors, the primary tradeoff is between supporting a niche cause in community relations and the reality of high administrative costs relative to program output.
